fields.h1: Build a Wine Tasting Form Template That Scores Every Pour
fields.hero_description: Build a wine tasting form template guests fill on their phones, with each wine's scores added up once the last guest is in.
fields.features_heading: What a Printed Score Sheet Leaves Out
fields.features_subheading: A printed sheet holds one guest's notes. Emergent builds a wine tasting form that puts every score in one table.
fields.feature_1:
A score sheet for every pour

Each wine gets its own screen with fields for appearance, nose, palate, and finish, then a score. Guests tap through to the next wine, and the form keeps their place.
fields.feature_2:
Bottles known only by a letter

Label the bottles A to F and the form shows guests only the letter. Names and prices stay in your table, out of sight, until you open the reveal after the last score.
fields.feature_3:
Totals per wine on your dashboard

The app adds up every guest's score for each wine and ranks all 6 bottles on a dashboard. You see which bottle leads, and by how many points, before the first guest asks.
fields.feature_4:
A buy box beside each wine

Put a buy box next to every wine on the flight. A guest's picks reach the counter tablet as one order under her name, and staff bag the bottles before she stands up.
fields.feature_5:
Results sent to Slack or email

Send the final tally to Slack or by email when the tasting closes. A shop owner reads which wine guests picked most, and a host gets the full ranking to read out loud.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can move to your own host

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and host the form anywhere. Every tasting note stays in a database you own, ready for your next flight.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Hosts, Four Ways to Pour
fields.tab_content_1:
Bottle C wins it on 35 of 40 points

Saffiyah Tamsell wraps 6 bottles in paper bags and marks them A to F before 8 friends arrive. Each guest scores every wine from 1 to 5 on a phone, and the form shows only the letter. When the last score lands, her dashboard ranks the bottles. Bottle C leads with 35 of 40 points, and the reveal shows it is the Garnacha.
fields.tab_content_2:
Into a bag at the counter go her 2 bottles

Each guest at Vellacourt Winery confirms she is 21 or older on the first screen, a check the winery asks for. The flight has 4 wines. One guest rates them on her phone and ticks buy on the Syrah and the Viognier. Her 2 bottles show up as an order on the counter tablet, and staff bag them while she finishes.
fields.tab_content_3:
From 9 of 12 students, a long finish on wine 3

Twelve students taste 5 wines in Yevette Nkemdirim's Tuesday class at Brisenbach Wine School. For each one, they fill in appearance, nose, palate, and finish. Her table lines up all 12 notes on a wine side by side. On wine 3, 9 of 12 students marked the finish long, so she starts with the other 3.
fields.tab_content_4:
After 14 votes, Grenache goes back on order

Seven bottles open each Thursday at Sorrel Lane Bottle Shop, and 22 guests came this week. Each guest picks one favorite before leaving. At close, the tally posts to the shop's #buying channel in Slack. Owner Ines Lindqvara reads that 14 of 22 chose the Grenache and orders 2 more cases.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Wine Tasting Form Template
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a wine tasting form template that scores each pour and ranks the wines, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Hide the labels for honest scores
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Plan what follows the last pour
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose the scale before you write a single question. Five points is quick for friends at a party. A class or a buying panel may want 20 or 100 points, but every wine poured that night has to use the same one.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Bag or wrap each bottle, give it a letter, and use only the letter on the form. Keep the real names in your table, and switch on the reveal once the last guest submits. Guests then judge the wine, not the price tag.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Offer finish as short, medium, or long, and body as light, medium, or full. Picked answers can be counted, and typed ones cannot. Keep one free-text box per wine for whatever a guest wants to say in their own words.
fields.howto_step_4_des: A tasting room can put a buy option on every wine, and a shop can ask for one favorite before guests leave. At a home party, the score alone may be enough, and a shorter form gets finished.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Put the link where guests sit
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send the link to every phone or print it on a card at each place setting. Each guest gets their own entry. Nobody shares a sheet, and no score has to be typed in later from paper.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Choose who sees the results and where. A host can read the ranking on the dashboard. A shop owner can get the tally in a Slack channel or an email once the last guest leaves, ready for the next order.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run the form once with a single bottle and two people before the real night. Check that the scores add up and that the reveal stays hidden until the last guest submits, then send the link out.

faq_plan.q: What is a wine tasting form template?
faq_plan.a: A wine tasting form template is a ready-made sheet or online form for scoring wines at a tasting. It gives every wine the same questions about color, aroma, taste, and finish, plus a score. Guests' notes can then be compared side by side.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a wine tasting form template?
faq_plan.a: Describe the tasting to Emergent's AI form builder: how many wines and which scoring scale. Say whether the labels stay hidden. Emergent builds the form and its database, plus a dashboard that ranks the wines. Change anything later by asking in plain English.

faq_plan.q: What should a wine tasting form template ask about each wine?
faq_plan.a: Ask the same things of every wine: how it looks, how it smells, how it tastes, how long the finish lasts, and a score. Put the wine's letter or name at the top. Keep each block short, because a guest tasting 6 wines answers it 6 times.

faq_plan.q: What scoring scale works best on a wine tasting form template?
faq_plan.a: A 1 to 5 score works best for a casual tasting, because guests can fill it in between sips. Critics use 100 points, and Wine Spectator's scale describes 90 to 94 as "Outstanding: a wine of superior character and style." Pick one scale and use it for every wine.

faq_plan.q: How do I run a blind tasting with a wine tasting form template?
faq_plan.a: Hide each label under foil and give each bottle a letter. Put only those letters on the form. Reveal the names after every score is in. Critics work this way too: at Wine Spectator, "Finished wines, reviewed from bottle in blind tastings, are given a single score."

faq_plan.q: Can guests fill out a wine tasting form template on their phones?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Put the link on the table or send it before the tasting, and each guest opens the form on their own phone. Every entry lands in one table, with no paper sheets to collect at the end. An Emergent form has no response caps. A 60-guest tasting fits as well as a dinner for 6.

faq_plan.q: How many wines should a wine tasting form template cover?
faq_plan.a: Keep a home tasting to 6 to 8 wines. Guests then finish the form with attention left for the last glass. For a class, match the form to the wines on that night's syllabus, and add a section for each one rather than one long page.

faq_plan.q: How do I add up the scores from a wine tasting form template?
faq_plan.a: Total each wine's scores across all guests, or average them if some guests skipped a wine. Doing it by hand from paper takes a while after a long night. Emergent builds a dashboard that adds the scores and ranks the wines once the last guest submits.

faq_plan.q: Should a wine tasting form template ask guests which bottles they want to buy?
faq_plan.a: Yes, at a tasting room or a shop, where a buy option beside each wine turns a guest's notes into an order staff can fill. At a party with friends, leave it off and keep the form to tasting notes and scores.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep the notes from a wine tasting form template between events?
faq_plan.a: Save every entry to a database instead of paper, with the date and the wine's name on each row. Next time, you can compare how the same guests scored a grape or a producer. With Emergent, the notes live in a database you own, and paid plans export the code to your GitHub repository.

plan.angle: The top 10 for wine tasting form template is printable score sheets and placemats (Pinterest, Etsy, a few free PDFs) that list wine name, appearance, nose, palate, finish and a score. A sheet like that stops at the table. This page shows the form after the pour: blind scores that add up into a reveal, a tasting room flight where guests mark the bottles they want to take home, a class instructor reading 12 sets of notes side by side, and a bottle shop that reorders from its guests' favorites. The how-to and FAQ cover what printables skip: picking a scale, running it blind, and keeping every score in one table.
